title: Laboratory sources that do facility-class coherent X-ray crystallography

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a coherent hard-X-ray source that a university or company laboratory could afford, house and operate, while supporting atomic-resolution, time-resolved crystallography with dependable experimental throughput. It would let researchers measure changes in crystal structures on very short timescales using a local instrument. The target combines source brightness, coherence, pulse duration, stability and sustained usability; producing compact hard-X-ray pulses alone does not establish that combination.

Relevant foundations include compact inverse-Compton sources, which generate X-rays by scattering laser light from energetic electrons, and compact free-electron-laser projects intended to produce coherent radiation. The supplied ASU commissioning paper documents partially coherent hard-X-ray pulses, while the companion compact FEL presentation describes a coherent 0.25–2.5 keV project under construction at presentation time. These are distinct technical steps toward the proposed capability, rather than demonstrations of the complete laboratory crystallography system.

significance.text: If the required performance, affordability and reliability were achieved, the direct consequence would be more local experimental capacity and greater freedom to build dedicated instruments around a source. Researchers could integrate accelerator, laser and X-ray beamline operation around particular experiments. ASU's institutional account describes major XFEL access as booked years ahead with short experimental allocations, supporting this access motivation, although it is not a comprehensive survey of facility availability.

Conditional impact assessment: widespread deployment could allow many groups to iterate daily on experiments that currently depend on scheduled facility access. That would also require manageable operating costs, suitable staffing, reliable sample delivery and effective data workflows. The Bessemer process and transistor are useful analogies for broadening access to a powerful capability, but they do not establish an equivalent historical impact or predict adoption.

Scope synthesis: the demanding target is the combination of atomic resolution, femtosecond structural measurements and dependable throughput. Coherent imaging is a broader family of methods, so its entire availability should not be equated with access to atomic-resolution femtosecond crystallography. A source that merely reproduces conventional laboratory diffraction would not satisfy this proposal. Brighter storage rings could improve shared facilities, but that is a different deployment model. A successful source would also leave separate problems in sample preparation, structure inference and reaction initiation to be solved.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability in the supplied demonstrations is a practical laboratory system that delivers coherent hard-X-ray radiation with sufficient brightness, short pulses, stability and useful shot rate to support the full crystallographic target. The ASU inverse-Compton paper establishes compact hard-X-ray production and reports pulses lasting a few hundred femtoseconds, but describes them as partially coherent. The companion FEL presentation targets coherent radiation at 0.25–2.5 keV, rather than demonstrating the proposed hard-X-ray operation. Neither source establishes the complete performance combination.

Engineering synthesis: shrinking the source must preserve the beam properties needed at the sample. For accelerator-based approaches, this means controlling electron-beam quality and stability, maintaining precise laser–electron timing and alignment where required, and transporting the resulting X-rays without losing the useful coherence or photon delivery. A working instrument must also synchronize excitation or mixing, sample delivery, detectors and data acquisition. A favorable source specification is insufficient if fluctuations or experimental losses prevent collection of interpretable time-resolved diffraction data.

Practical synthesis: building-scale size does not establish university-laboratory affordability. Installed cost, shielding and other infrastructure, power consumption, maintenance, specialist staffing and sustained uptime all affect whether the source can be used routinely. The supplied evidence does not establish an affordable implementation, a numerical cost boundary or a reliable completion date. The development duration and cost therefore remain uncertain; describing it as a definite long engineering program would imply more forecasting confidence than the record supports.

current_state.text: The supplied European XFEL comparison lists facility lengths of 3.4 km for European XFEL and 3 km for LCLS, with peak-brilliance entries of 5 × 10^33 and 2 × 10^33, respectively. These are facility lengths, not identified accelerator lengths. The retained comparison table does not state brilliance units, limiting direct physical comparisons with separately reported source specifications.

The 2024 ASU CXLS commissioning paper lists design values of 2–20 keV photon energy, 5 × 10^6 photons per pulse in 0.1% bandwidth, and peak brilliance of 3 × 10^19 ph/(s 0.1% mm² mrad²). It separately reports an achieved commissioning output of about 5 × 10^5 photons per shot at reduced electron charge and laser power. The design brilliance should not be presented as an achieved commissioning measurement. The paper documents compact, partially coherent hard-X-ray pulses with durations of a few hundred femtoseconds.

Comparing the listed European XFEL and LCLS peak-brilliance numbers with the CXLS design number gives ratios of approximately 1.7 × 10^14 and 6.7 × 10^13, respectively: roughly fourteen orders of magnitude. This is a conditional numerical comparison, requiring consistent units and brilliance definitions that cannot be confirmed from the retained European XFEL table. It also compares facility entries with a compact-source design target; it does not measure the relative performance of complete crystallography experiments.

ASU News reported the first protein structure obtained with CXLS on September 26, 2025. The supplied Mark Holl presentation additionally identifies a proteinase K structure at 2 Å resolution. This resolution statement should be retained as a reported result, but it remains a presentation claim: the review did not inspect the underlying map or presentation figures. Neither retained ASU account supplies a PDB accession or a peer-reviewed report of that structure. The supplied material therefore supports a reported protein-crystallography milestone without establishing previously unknown structures, femtosecond time resolution or the complete proposed capability.

The Holl presentation describes the companion ASU CXFEL as a coherent 0.25–2.5 keV source being constructed under an NSF program. This establishes the stated construction status of that soft-X-ray project at presentation time. Its presentation date is not established in the supplied review, so it does not determine the project's status on November 1, 2026, or the status of compact FEL projects generally.

The earlier research attributes to Barber and collaborators a July 29, 2025 Physical Review Letters result involving plasma-driven FEL gain exceeding 1,000-fold at 420 nm and 1 Hz, without claimed saturation or X-ray operation. No source text was retained for the supplied citation, so the review could not assess the date, numerical performance or saturation characterization. These remain unverified details in this record, rather than established achievements or disproven claims. Even if confirmed as described, visible-wavelength gain would be a precursor result rather than a demonstration of saturated coherent hard-X-ray operation.

Evidence-bound synthesis: the supplied materials establish compact hard-X-ray production, an institutionally reported protein structure and a coherent soft-X-ray construction project. They do not demonstrate the full proposed laboratory capability. The supplied record contains no documented freshness search establishing worldwide status as of November 1, 2026; consequently, it cannot support a categorical claim that no laboratory anywhere has achieved it. This limitation does not negate the dated 2024 and 2025 results.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: two independent laboratories should each use a coherent hard-X-ray source housed within a building to solve and deposit previously unknown room-temperature, time-resolved crystal structures at atomic resolution. Each demonstration should report achieved spatial resolution, temporal resolution and source coherence, together with enough experimental information to assess the structural conclusions. These are proposed tests of the concept, not published consensus requirements.
completion_criteria.label: Two labs deposit unknown atomic-resolution, room-temperature time-resolved structures

completion_criteria.text: Proposed breadth and reproducibility test: at least one demonstration should use a non-photoactive mix-and-inject experiment, extending the test beyond systems that can be initiated with light. Independent installations and reproducible structural conclusions would provide stronger evidence than first light, a single commissioning protein structure or a visible-wavelength gain curve. The demonstrated structures and timing range would define the supported breadth; finite experiments would not establish applicability to every crystal, reaction or timescale.
completion_criteria.label: Non-photoactive mix-and-inject experiments yield reproducible structural conclusions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practicality test: report uptime, usable shots per day, completed experimental throughput and stability over months, alongside installed and operating costs, staffing, maintenance and infrastructure requirements. These records should show whether the system is practical for its intended laboratory users. Building size and raw shot counts alone would not establish affordability or scientific productivity. Numerical acceptance boundaries for cost, resolution, timing and reliability would need to be declared for the intended applications; the supplied sources establish no universal thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Report sustained experimental productivity, full resource costs and application-specific boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CRX-01, atomic-resolution imaging of a single non-crystalline molecule before destruction, and CRX-08, ab initio structure of matter that exists only once, could benefit from improved access to intense short X-ray pulses. Their central challenges concern obtaining enough information from non-crystalline or non-repeatable targets. Demonstrating time-resolved crystallography on crystals would not establish either capability, and a local source would not by itself solve their measurement or reconstruction problems.

Roster-based synthesis: CRX-02, chemically complete structures of bulk amorphous solids, and CRX-04, atomic ensembles measured from total X-ray scattering, concern recovering structural information from scattering data. CRX-05, experimental many-electron quantum states of real crystals, and CRX-09, routine crystallographic protonation-state measurement, concern additional electronic or chemical information. A better laboratory source could improve access or data collection, but source performance alone would not establish the information content, sensitivity or inference methods required by these distinct concepts.

Roster-based synthesis: CRX-06, atomic movies of elementary chemical steps without a photo-trigger, has the closest experimental overlap with the proposed non-photoactive mix-and-inject demonstration. CRX-10 concerns the enabling source and its practical availability; CRX-06 additionally requires suitable reaction initiation, timing and structural interpretation. One successful mixing experiment would demonstrate a useful intersection without establishing general access to elementary chemical steps. CRX-12, continuous atomic-resolution crystallography inside working devices and static extreme environments, likewise could benefit from a dedicated local source while retaining separate requirements for sample environments, access geometry and continuous measurement.

Roster-based synthesis: CRX-03, predicting which molecular crystal will form with chemical accuracy, and CRX-07, experimentally selecting a chosen crystal form, address prediction and control of crystallization. CRX-11, diffraction-quality crystals of arbitrary macromolecules on demand, addresses sample availability, while CRX-13, suppressing defects, twins and disorder through a growth rulebook, addresses crystal quality. Easier structural measurement could support work on all four, but a compact source would not supply their predictive or growth capabilities. Conversely, improved samples could make a source more productive without demonstrating CRX-10's required radiation performance.

Technical relationship synthesis: compact inverse-Compton sources and coherent soft-X-ray FEL projects are relevant foundations for CRX-10, while brighter shared storage rings offer another route to improved experimental capacity. These approaches overlap in enabling X-ray science but differ in coherence, photon energy, pulse properties and deployment. Their individual milestones should remain distinguishable from the proposed combination of laboratory practicality and facility-class coherent hard-X-ray crystallography.

change_log.change: Preserved CRX-10's identity and framed the innovation as a proposed combination of coherent hard-X-ray performance, crystallographic usefulness and laboratory practicality.
change_log.reason: Existing precursor achievements do not demonstrate the complete target, and incomplete supporting evidence does not invalidate the concept.

change_log.change: Corrected the European XFEL and LCLS dimensions from accelerator lengths to facility lengths.
change_log.reason: The supplied comparison table labels the measured quantity as facility length.

change_log.change: Separated CXLS design specifications from achieved commissioning output and made the fourteen-order brilliance comparison conditional.
change_log.reason: The design table and commissioning result describe different performance categories, while the retained European XFEL table omits brilliance units.

change_log.change: Integrated the reported proteinase K result at 2 Å resolution while preserving its presentation-level evidence and missing accession and publication details.
change_log.reason: The earlier account omitted useful resolution information; the review also establishes limits on independent assessment of that result.

change_log.change: Restricted the compact FEL construction statement to the documented ASU project at presentation time.
change_log.reason: An undated presentation cannot establish current status or characterize all compact FEL projects.

change_log.change: Retained the plasma-FEL numerical claims as explicitly unverified details.
change_log.reason: No source text was captured for their assessment. Missing evidence neither confirms nor refutes the claimed result.

change_log.change: Replaced categorical worldwide absence and literature-search negatives with bounded statements about the supplied evidence.
change_log.reason: The record contains no documented freshness search establishing worldwide status as of November 1, 2026.

change_log.change: Separated direct access benefits from conditional deployment effects and qualified the historical analogies and coherent-imaging access claim.
change_log.reason: Widespread daily iteration requires costs, staffing and workflows beyond source performance; the sources do not establish confinement of all coherent imaging or storage-ring oversubscription.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed completion criteria to include measured coherence, temporal performance, sustained throughput and practical operating requirements.
change_log.reason: Building size and shot counts alone would not test the full scientific and accessibility goals.

change_log.change: Used the supplied roster to explain relationships with the other CRX concepts as title-based synthesis.
change_log.reason: The review lacked their definitions, but the final inputs provide titles sufficient for bounded comparisons without inventing detailed requirements.

unresolved_issues: The complete capability's worldwide status as of November 1, 2026 remains unestablished by the supplied evidence.
The European XFEL comparison's brilliance units and compatibility with the CXLS definition remain unconfirmed.
The reported 2 Å proteinase K structure lacks a supplied PDB accession, peer-reviewed structure report and inspected underlying map.
The Holl presentation date and subsequent ASU CXFEL construction or operating status remain unestablished.
The plasma-driven FEL citation's reported date, gain, wavelength, repetition rate and saturation characterization require source text before verification.
No demonstrated installed cost, operating cost, staffing model or affordability threshold establishes practicality for an ordinary university or company laboratory.
Application-specific acceptance boundaries for atomic resolution, temporal resolution, coherence, throughput and sustained reliability remain to be defined.

Related-concept comparisons are limited to the supplied roster titles. The review's recommendation to defer all such comparisons was not adopted because those titles permit useful, explicitly qualified distinctions; detailed technical overlaps remain unresolved.

prerequisites.reason: Laboratory time-resolved crystallography requires the laboratory-scale coherent hard X-ray source supplied by OPT-04.
